items.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
items.content_html:
Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile

Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.

Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”

items.title: The new Bundesliga season is here, but has the glow gone?
items.content_html: Another Bundesliga season arrives, but are the golden years of Germany's top football league already over, and what can it do to change its course?

items.title: Star violinist Anne-Sophie Mutter: 50 years on stage
items.content_html: Anne-Sophie Mutter constantly reinvents herself. For her 50th onstage anniversary, the star violinist is surprising audiences with sounds from around the world and never-before-recorded commissions.

items.title: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
items.content_html: "Immune hubs" that actively defend the brain have been discovered in mouse skull marrow. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

items.title: Spiraling health costs force Iranians to delay care
items.content_html: A single chemotherapy session in Iran can cost six times the monthly minimum wage. As drug prices soar and medicine is in short supply, doctors say more patients are delaying or abandoning treatment.

items.title: Sydney Marathon medal wrongly shows German landmark
items.content_html: A medal minted for finishers in the Sydney Marathon features a skyline of the city — with one landmark from rather far away. Organizers say the muddle only makes the medal "a little more unique."

items.title: Why Germany's gas storage levels are so low
items.content_html: Germany's gas storage facilities are only 50% full as traders bet that wholesale prices will fall if the Iran war ends. With around three months until winter, DW asks whether the country can refill its reserves in time.

items.title: How Europe can better protect against extreme wildfires
items.content_html: In another summer of European wildfires that have even seen wetlands burning, scientists say the situation is set to worsen in the future. What's needed is fire prevention and climate protection.

items.title: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life in prison
items.content_html: A Chinese court ordered the former billionaire's assets to be confiscated and fined Evergrande-related companies billions of dollars.

items.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
items.content_html: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

items.title: How to grow food for more people in a hotter world
items.content_html: Inside futuristic labs, plants are scanned, stressed and analyzed. The aim is to use the results to produce plant strains that can better serve a growing population in a warming world.

items.title: Do not inhale! How wildfire smoke 'affects the whole body'
items.content_html: Wildfires destroy lives and livelihoods. But survivors and firefighters also suffer long-term harm to their health. A growing body of research suggests particulate matter (PM2.5) in wildfire smoke is a major culprit.
